summary:
Visual audit of OpenEtch at http://127.0.0.1:7979, run in tab "seed" at 1920x1080, 1440x900, 1280x800, 1280x720, 1024x768, 820x1180 and the mobile preset (375x812; the preset is not 390x844). I checked dark and light themes, then reset the tab to the desktop preset and left it open.

What already works:
- Pointer-event editing: draw, select, move and resize are all fine, and the left-to-right marquee encloses.
- Undo appears in the Fusion-style timeline as a ghosted chip.
- Edits sync live between two tabs.
- Below 1024 px the side panels become drawers with a scrim.
- The Preferences dialog has Text size, Icon size and Handle size sliders.
- Menu items are 44 px tall. The Rectangle tool's hint says "tap for 20 mm".
- The Laser workspace is lean, and Start/Stop sit near the top of its panel.
- Light and dark themes both render cleanly.

The biggest problems:
1. **Too little canvas on a MacBook.** Fixed bars take about 331 px of height, and the side panels are fixed at 272 + 320 px with no resizer or collapse rail. The canvas is 688x423 at 1280x800, 688x343 at 1280x720 (a real Safari window), and 432x381 on iPad landscape.
2. **Toolbar hidden off the right edge.** The ribbon needs 2094 px at every width. Even at 1920, Commands and the Properties panel toggle are off screen. At 1280 everything after Tools is hidden behind a thin scrollbar.
3. **File menu cut off.** It is 1337 px tall, cannot scroll and has no max-height. On any screen under about 1340 px tall, Devices, Preferences, Material Library, Find My Laser, Batch run and Job log cannot be reached.
4. **Top bar breaks on iPad portrait and phone.** At 820 px the Window button covers the Laser workspace tab. On the phone the workspace switcher shrinks to 6 px and STOP is pushed off screen (21 of 82 px visible).
5. **STOP blocked by dialogs.** Every modal backdrop covers the STOP button; a hit-test at STOP's centre returns `.modal-backdrop`.
6. **Touch gaps.** One finger on empty canvas pans, so touch has no marquee selection. There are no on-screen Shift/Ctrl/Alt toggles. Right-click menus have no long-press alternative, which matters most on iPad Safari. Resize handles are 8 px to see and 16 px to hit, and many controls are under 44 px.
7. **No full-screen or app-window mode.** There is no full-screen toggle, no web manifest, no icon and no apple-touch-icon.

Smaller issues:
- Escape leaves a toolbar dropdown open but clears the selection.
- The frame-options popover runs 157 px below the window and covers Start.
- The numeric bar wraps and cuts off its values.
- The properties panel is 3089 px tall and repeats controls.
- Some labels show developer wording.

Interference during the audit: another agent opened a second tab (tab-1) in the browser pane. It also brought that tab to the front, switched it to the Laser workspace and resized it to 1280x720 and then 1180x820. So I ran everything else with tabId "seed". The second tab shares the same engine document, which now holds 3 objects (two rectangles and the text "Hello").

findings.problem: Fixed bars take about 331 px of height and the side panels about 592 px of width, which leaves a small canvas on a MacBook. There is no compact mode, no panel resizer and no collapse-to-icon-rail.
findings.evidence: Measured heights: topbar 48, doc tabs 31, toolbar 91 (72 px buttons plus a scrollbar), numeric bar 50 (96 when it wraps below about 850 px of centre width), palette 29, timeline 58, status bar 24. Canvas (.center-stage) size: 688x423 at 1280x800 (28% of the screen); 688x343 at 1280x720, the real Safari viewport of a 1280x800 MacBook; 848x569 at 1440x900. The left Browser panel is a fixed 272 px and mostly empty with a small tree; the right panel is a fixed 320 px. CSS has no max-height media queries and nothing that resizes the panels.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact density for heights under about 900 px: a 40-48 px icon toolbar with labels as tooltips, the numeric bar merged into the toolbar or the top of the properties panel, and the doc tabs merged into the topbar. Let the palette and timeline collapse to thin strips (Fusion keeps its timeline at about 32 px). Make the side panels resizable, collapsible to an icon rail, and auto-collapsed when the canvas would drop below about 700 px. Add a 'focus canvas' toggle (Tab or F11 style) that hides every panel.

findings.problem: The ribbon is 2094 px wide at every viewport, so many tools sit off screen behind a thin horizontal scrollbar that gives no hint anything is there. That includes the only toolbar toggle for the Properties panel.
findings.evidence: Toolbar scrollWidth is 2094 px against clientWidth 1280, 1440 and even 1920. At 1920: Commands at x=1941 and the Properties toggle at x=2024 are off screen. At 1440: Place, Array, Delete, the whole align/distribute/group/flip cluster, the snap toggles, Filled view, Commands and Properties are hidden. At 1280 everything after 'Tools' is hidden. At 1024 everything after 'Measure' is hidden. 'Laser Tools' wraps to two lines in a 47 px button.
findings.recommendation: Use a Fusion-style tabbed or grouped ribbon (Create / Modify / Arrange / Laser), with each group collapsing to a dropdown when space runs out (a priority-plus overflow '»' menu). Move the panel toggles (Browser, Properties) to fixed positions at the edges of the topbar, or to an always-visible rail, not the scrolling ribbon. Shrink buttons to icon-only with tooltips in compact mode.

findings.problem: The File menu cannot scroll and has no max-height, so its lower items are off screen and unreachable on a laptop, iPad or phone.
findings.evidence: The File .menu is 1337 px tall from top 47; scrollHeight equals clientHeight, and wheel scrolling over it does nothing. At 1280x800 the last visible item is 'Notes…'. 'Restore from autosave', 'Import options', 'Preferences and bundles', 'Devices…', 'Download .openetch', 'New tab', 'Preferences…', 'Edit hotkeys', 'Material Library', 'Find My Laser / Add galvo…', 'Batch run…' and 'Job log…' are below the bottom edge. It is the same on the 375x812 phone. The .menu rule (styles.css:467) has no max-height or overflow, while ctx-menu (styles.css:1789) does have max-height: calc(100vh - 8px).
findings.recommendation: Give .menu max-height: calc(100dvh - top - 8px) and overflow-y: auto. Also shorten the menu: it has 26 items with duplicates ('Preferences and bundles…' and 'Preferences…'; Material Library and Devices also live elsewhere). Split it into File / Machine / Settings, or use submenus. Use about 32 px rows with a pointer:fine query and keep 44 px for coarse pointers.

findings.area: Topbar on narrow screens (STOP / workspace switch)
findings.problem: Below about 900 px wide the topbar actions (flex: none, 566 px) overrun the workspace switcher. On iPad portrait the Laser tab is covered and cannot be tapped. On the phone the switcher collapses to 6 px and the STOP button is pushed mostly off screen.
findings.evidence: At 820x1180, elementFromPoint at the centre of the Laser workspace button returns the 'Window' button, because topbar-actions starts at x=246 and Laser spans x=239-301. At 375x812: .workspaces is 6 px wide; .btn-stop sits at left 354 with width 82 in a 375 px viewport (21 px visible); topbar scrollWidth is 436. The screenshot shows only a red sliver at the right edge. The CSS comment at styles.css:673 says the switcher shrinks 'before STOP ever does', but .topbar-actions is flex: none, so STOP overflows instead.
findings.recommendation: Make STOP a fixed-size item that is never clipped (outside the flex overflow, or position: sticky right). On narrow widths, fold Window, Help, theme, preferences, undo and redo into one '⋯' menu and show the connection status as just the dot. Keep Design/Laser as a two-icon segmented control. On phones, consider a bottom tab bar (Design / Laser / Layers / Properties) with a permanent STOP.

findings.problem: Every modal backdrop sits on top of the topbar Emergency STOP, so STOP cannot be clicked while any dialog is open (Devices, Preferences, Cut settings and so on).
findings.evidence: With the Devices dialog open at 1280x800, elementFromPoint at the centre of .btn-stop returns 'modal-backdrop', and the STOP button is visibly dimmed under the overlay. The cut-settings and Preferences dialogs also cover it (modal top 16 px, backdrop covers the whole viewport).
findings.recommendation: Exclude the topbar STOP from the backdrop: give the topbar or .btn-stop a z-index above .modal-backdrop, or start the backdrop below the topbar. Also make Esc and Space with a modal open never swallow a global stop hotkey, if one exists.

findings.problem: On touch, one finger on empty canvas always pans, so there is no marquee selection. There are no on-screen modifier toggles, so Shift-add, Ctrl-toggle, constrain and snap-off are impossible. Every right-click-only menu has no long-press alternative.
findings.evidence: Viewport.tsx:604-607: 'if (e.pointerType === "touch") { // One finger on empty space pans'. A grep finds no long-press handling and no sticky modifier UI in web/src. There are 14 onContextMenu handlers (canvas Viewport.tsx:1077, Timeline.tsx:180, BrowserPanel, CutsLayers, MaterialLibrary, ArtLibrary, PagesDock, Dock/DockHost). Timeline chip tooltips say 'Right-click for more' and layer rows say 'right-click for more'. iPad Safari does not fire contextmenu on long-press.
findings.recommendation: Add a small floating touch toolbar on coarse pointers with sticky Shift / Ctrl / Alt toggles and a Select/Pan mode switch (or two-finger pan with one-finger marquee, as in Procreate/Shapr3D). Add a long-press (about 500 ms, within the tap slop) that opens the same context menu everywhere onContextMenu is used. Also show a '⋯' button on timeline chips and on tree and layer rows.

findings.problem: Many controls are far below 44 px on touch, and the on-canvas transform handles do not grow for coarse pointers.
findings.evidence: At 375x812 with a coarse pointer: scale handles are 8 px to see and 16x16 to hit, rotate handles 18x18 (Viewport.tsx:1169/1179 hpx(8)/hpx(9); HANDLE_PX = 8 in useDesignUi.tsx:117). Reference-point anchor grid buttons are 13x13. Palette swatches are 18x22. Doc tab '+' is 26x24 and the doc tab is 26 px tall. Status bar buttons (zoom %, units) are 20 px tall. Timeline transport is 36x36. Arrange/align mini buttons are 26x24. Ruler unit button is 20x20. The --tap variable is 40px (styles.css:81). On a selected 10.8x3.6 mm text, the handles completely cover the text even at desktop size.
findings.recommendation: Under (pointer: coarse), set --tap to 44px, scale the handle hit areas to at least 32-44 px (a default handle scale of about 2 on coarse pointers), enlarge swatches to 32 px with a scrolling palette, and use 44 px rows in the status bar and timeline. When a selection is small on screen, place the handles outside the bounds (min box size) so the object stays visible.

findings.problem: There is no full-screen mode and no installable app shell, so the app cannot run as a title-bar-only window. The owner listed this as a goal.
findings.evidence: No button, menu item or title matches 'full screen' (searched the DOM and requestFullscreen in source). The Window menu lists only panels and 'Reset to default layout'. index.html has only charset, viewport and apple-mobile-web-app-capable: no <link rel=manifest>, no icon or favicon, no apple-touch-icon, no theme-color, and web/public does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Full screen' (F11 / Ctrl+Cmd+F) to the Window menu and as a topbar icon, using element.requestFullscreen() with the webkit prefix for iPad. Add manifest.webmanifest (display: standalone or window-controls-overlay, name, icons, theme_color) plus apple-touch-icon and apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style. Chrome/Edge 'Install' or 'Open as window' and Safari 'Add to Dock' / 'Add to Home Screen' then give a chrome-less window. Note that full PWA install in Chrome needs a secure context, so on plain-http LAN document 'Create shortcut → Open as window' or serve a self-signed https option.

findings.problem: At 1024 px the panels stay docked (the drawer breakpoint is max-width: 1023px), which leaves a 432 px wide canvas. Hiding the Browser panel does not re-fit the view, so the top of the field is clipped.
findings.evidence: At 1024x768: canvas 432x381, numeric bar wraps to two rows (96 px), palette scrolls horizontally (670/432). After toggling the Browser panel off, the canvas is wider but the field's top edge sits above the visible area and the fit buttons overlap the field. NARROW_QUERY = "(max-width: 1023px)" in App.tsx:106.
findings.recommendation: Choose drawers from the space the canvas would get rather than viewport width alone (for example, docked panels only when the canvas would be at least about 700 px wide). Or switch at 1279 px and use overlay drawers or an icon rail on iPad landscape. Re-fit the view, or keep its centre, when panel visibility changes.

findings.area: Phone: properties drawer auto-opens over the canvas
findings.problem: On narrow layouts, selecting or drawing a shape slides in the 320 px Properties drawer with a scrim, covering about 85% of the phone screen and the object being edited. The next canvas tap only closes the drawer.
findings.evidence: At 375x812, after drawing a rectangle the right panel (.panel-right.open, left 55, width 320) and .drawer-scrim cover the canvas, and the drawn shape is hidden. App.tsx:221: 'if (narrow && workspace === "design" && (s.objects.length > 0 || s.stock)) setRightOpen(true)'.
findings.recommendation: On phones use a bottom sheet with peek / half / full states that shows the key numeric fields (X/Y/W/H, layer) at peek height, and do not auto-expand it. Keep the selection visible: pan or zoom the canvas into the remaining space.

findings.problem: The X/Y/W/H inputs are too narrow and clip their values. The bar wraps onto a second or third row, which wastes vertical space. The inputs have no accessible labels.
findings.evidence: At 1280x800 the inputs are 45 px wide: X shows '-27.4' for -27.463, W shows '54.92' for 54.925, and '122.5' for 122.572. The bar is 96 px tall with 'mm | in' alone on row 2 (multi-select puts 'Rot by' on row 2). On the phone the bar is 135 px (three rows). read_page names the textboxes by their values (e.g. textbox "43.767"), not 'X'/'Y'.
findings.recommendation: Use min-width: 7ch inputs (or 8ch with the sign) and drop the inline 'mm' suffix inside the field, since the unit toggle already shows it. Put mm/in in the status bar only, which already has it. Add aria-labels. In compact mode merge the bar into the toolbar row.

findings.problem: With a shape selected, the right panel is a single 3089 px column (5.6 screens at 1280x800). Shape Properties sits below Pages, Cuts/Layers, the inline layer quick settings, Material Library, Art Library and Docking. The same layer and transform controls appear two or three times.
findings.evidence: At 1280x800: panel-body scrollHeight 3089 against clientHeight 548. The text shows Speed/Power/Passes/Frequency/Q-Pulse inline under Cuts/Layers, then again in the 'CUT SETTINGS' and 'Layer' blocks inside Shape Properties. X/Y/W/H/Rotation appear in both the numeric bar and Shape Properties. Selecting a shape does not scroll to its properties. The Q-Pulse placeholder is clipped ('source c').
findings.recommendation: Use Fusion-style tabs or an accordion where only one library is open at a time. Pin Shape Properties to the top, or auto-scroll to it, when something is selected. Drop the duplicated cut-settings block (keep the inline quick row plus 'All settings…'). Let the user dock libraries into the left panel.

findings.problem: The frame-style popover is absolutely positioned inside the Laser panel. It covers the Start and in-panel STOP buttons and runs 157 px below the viewport.
findings.evidence: At 1280x800, .frame-pop spans top 406 to bottom 957 with viewport height 800. The Pointer, Blanking and Live framing options are off screen until the panel is scrolled, and the popover sits over Start/STOP.
findings.recommendation: Open it as a flip-aware floating popover (above when there is no room below) with max-height and internal scroll, or as a collapsible section in the panel. Never cover STOP.

findings.problem: Pressing Escape while a toolbar dropdown (Edit) is open leaves the dropdown open and clears the canvas selection instead.
findings.evidence: With 1 object selected I opened Edit ▾ and pressed Escape. The status bar changed to 'Nothing selected' and the .menu element was still present; the screenshot shows the Edit dropdown still open.
findings.recommendation: Toolbar dropdowns (et-dropdown / lx-drop) should catch Escape, close themselves and stop propagation before the canvas Escape handler runs.

findings.problem: On the phone every status bar cell is truncated to the point of being useless. The timeline spends 176 px on its vertical label and transport, which leaves a 199 px strip. The status bar sits under the home-indicator safe area.
findings.evidence: At 375x812 the status bar reads 'X — Y...', 'Nothing selec...', 'Snap: obje...', '5...', 'mm · m...'. The timeline strip is 199 px wide starting at x=176. Safe-area bottom padding is applied to .timeline (styles.css:1632-1637), but the status bar comes after it in the grid.
findings.recommendation: On phones, hide the status bar or reduce it to the selection size, and move the safe-area padding to the last row. Collapse the timeline to a single scrubber row with transport in an overflow.

findings.problem: The Text tool's floating options bar (about 600x95 CSS px) and the tool hint banners sit over the top of the canvas, hiding part of the field on small screens. The red 'outside the galvo field' toast covers the zoom-fit buttons.
findings.evidence: At 1280x800 the 'New text' panel covers the top 20% of the 423 px canvas. The rectangle-tool hint ('Drag to draw a rectangle…') runs up to the fit buttons. The red warning toast at top right sits on top of the Fit field / Zoom to selection buttons.
findings.recommendation: Put tool options in a context strip that replaces the numeric bar while a tool is active, as Fusion does, instead of overlaying the canvas. Anchor toasts away from the canvas controls (bottom-centre above the palette).

findings.problem: Several labels show internal names instead of user-facing wording.
findings.evidence: Timeline chips are labelled 'rect', 'transform', 'text', with tooltips like 'object.transform move [55.782, -45.323] on obj-2'. The Machine and runs panel dumps raw keys: 'Field Height Mm 153.75', 'Focus Light false', 'Shutting Down false', 'Driver lmc'. The device select is clipped to 'ComMarker B6 MOPA 60W (E'. The Text object shows a path icon in the Browser tree. The Edit dropdown has no Select all / Delete / Duplicate / Undo.
findings.recommendation: Give each timeline chip an icon plus a friendly verb ('Rectangle', 'Move', 'Text "Hello"'), as in Fusion's feature icons. Show machine state as formatted rows (Focus light: Off) and hide debug fields behind an 'Advanced' toggle. Use a T icon for text. Fill out the Edit menu.

findings.problem: On reload the drawing tools (Text, Barcode, Line, Pen, Polygon, Edit nodes, Trim) briefly show disabled with no loading cue. In the light theme the grid is very faint, and the topbar stays dark while the rest of the UI is light.
findings.evidence: In the first light-theme screenshot after reload these tools were greyed out; a second later only Place, Array and Delete were disabled. The light-theme grid lines are barely visible against white.
findings.recommendation: Show a subtle loading spinner or skeleton, or keep the tools enabled and queue the action. Raise the light-theme grid contrast slightly. Decide on purpose whether the topbar follows the theme.

architecture_notes:
Layout lives in the CSS grid on .app (styles.css:294-304: rows 48px / doc tabs / toolbar / main / timeline / status). The panels are fixed widths (.panel 272px, .panel-right 320px), and they switch to drawers through a JS media query, NARROW_QUERY "(max-width: 1023px)" in App.tsx:106, which adds the .narrow class. App.tsx:221 auto-opens the right drawer on selection.

Responsive CSS is minimal. It is all max-width rules on small pieces (topbar shrink at 760 and 480, dialogs). There are no max-height queries, nothing for pointer: coarse (only a single pointer: fine rule), and no responsive rules for .toolbar, .main or the panels.

Touch handling:
- --tap is 40px (styles.css:81).
- Canvas handles come from hpx() in Viewport.tsx (8 px visible, 16 px hit) and scale only with the Preferences 'Handle and node size' slider.
- The touch branch in Viewport.tsx (~L604) maps one-finger drags on empty canvas to pan.
- There is no long-press handling; 14 onContextMenu handlers exist.

Menus:
- .menu (styles.css:467) has no max-height; .ctx-menu (styles.css:1789) does.
- Modal backdrop: styles.css:2192.
- Frame popover: components/job.css:150.
- Toolbar: components/Toolbar.tsx, a single horizontally scrolling flex row (scrollWidth 2094).
- index.html has no manifest or icons, and there is no web/public folder.

Concurrency note for the orchestrator: a second tab (tab-1) was opened in the shared browser pane by another actor during this audit. It switched to the Laser workspace and was resized, and it shares the engine document, which now holds two rectangles and a text "Hello". I used tabId "seed" explicitly from then on, and reset seed to preset desktop (dark colour scheme) at the end.

summary:
The shell is a single CSS grid on `.app` (styles.css:294). Its rows are: top bar 48px, document tabs, toolbar, main, timeline, status bar. `main` is a flex row: left panel at a fixed 272px, the canvas column, and the right panel at a fixed 320px. The app has one JS breakpoint (`NARROW_QUERY` "(max-width: 1023px)", App.tsx:26). Below 1024px it adds `.narrow`, which turns both panels into overlay drawers 86vw wide. The rest is a few CSS-only `max-width` tweaks at 900/760/640/600/560/480px. The numeric bar is the only part using a container query.

Colours are cleanly tokenised and dark mode works. Size, spacing, z-index and density are not tokenised. `--tap` is a fixed 40px for mouse and touch alike.

I measured against the running simulator (127.0.0.1:7979) at four sizes:
- **1280x720 (MacBook-class browser area):** the canvas gets 688x343px, about 26% of the window. Vertical chrome is 377px: topbar 48, a 31px doc-tab row with only one tab open, toolbar 91, numeric bar 96 (a wrap bug makes it three rows), palette 29, timeline 58, status 24. The toolbar content is 2094px wide in 1280px, so Arrange, Snap/View, Commands and the Properties panel toggle are off-screen. There is no visible scroll hint on macOS.
- **1024x700 (iPad landscape with Safari chrome):** both fixed panels stay docked, which leaves the canvas at 432x313. One pixel narrower, the whole layout flips to drawers.
- **375x812 (phone):** the STOP button is cut off the right edge: 61 of its 82px are past the viewport and clipped by `overflow: hidden` on `.app`. The Design/Laser switcher shrinks to 6px wide, so the Laser workspace can't really be reached. In the Laser workspace, the Machine drawer toggle sits at x=466–530, off-screen in the scrolling toolbar.

Nothing implements full screen or an app window: there is no Fullscreen API call, no web manifest, no theme-color and no icons.

Proposed architecture:
1. **Layout modes.** A `useLayoutMode()` hook sets `data-layout` = wide / compact / tablet / phone and `data-pointer` = fine / coarse on `<html>`. Preferences gets an override (Auto / Comfortable / Compact / Touch). Tokens and CSS key off these attributes instead of the single `.narrow` class.
2. **Density tokens.** Control height, gaps, bar heights and dock widths come from tokens per mode.
3. **Ribbon overflow.** A ResizeObserver collapses low-priority toolbar groups into Fusion-style group dropdowns ("CREATE ▾", "MODIFY ▾", "ARRANGE ▾"). The panel toggles move out of the scrolling area.
4. **Docks.** Resizable side docks with persisted widths. Each dock area gets pinned / auto-hide-rail / hidden states, stored in the existing layout.ts store. The compact default layout uses tab groups instead of six stacked docks.
5. **Timeline.** It can collapse, and it merges with the status bar in compact mode.
6. **Full screen.** A Full screen toggle plus a focus-mode hotkey, and a manifest with standalone display for an app-like window.
7. **Phone shell.** A separate shell that reuses the existing components: top bar with STOP always visible, full-bleed canvas, bottom tab bar (Canvas / Layers / Job / More) and bottom sheets. Its scope is monitoring, framing, Start (still gated by the app's approval / foot switch), layer power and speed, simple move and align, import and run history.

All of this fits the current plain-CSS and React codebase in five small phases (see architecture_notes). No UI library is needed.

findings.problem: On phone widths the top bar overflows and the always-visible STOP button is cut off past the right edge of the screen.
findings.evidence: At 375x812 `.btn-stop` spans x=354–436, so 61 of its 82px are off-screen, and `.app { overflow: hidden }` (styles.css:294-304) hides the rest. The top bar's scrollWidth is 436 vs 375. `.topbar-actions { flex: none }` (styles.css:680) holds Window, theme, prefs, Help, undo, redo, the connection status and STOP, about 372px, so it can't shrink. The 480px media block (styles.css:2453) only trims padding.
findings.recommendation: Make STOP an un-shrinkable last item outside the overflowing group: `.topbar-actions { flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0 }` with a `.topbar-stop { flex: none }` wrapper. Below about 900px, fold Window, Help, theme and Preferences into one overflow menu, and below about 600px fold undo and redo into it too. Add a dev-only check in the layout hook that warns in the console when the STOP button's bounding rect leaves the viewport on resize. That makes this kind of regression visible.

findings.problem: On a phone the Design/Laser workspace switcher shrinks to 6px wide, so you can't really switch to the Laser workspace, which is the one you need for monitoring and starting jobs.
findings.evidence: At 375px, `.topbar .workspaces` measures 6px wide with scrollWidth 111 (styles.css:674: `min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none`). Its siblings are flex:none, so it absorbs all the shrinking.
findings.recommendation: Give the switcher a floor (`flex: none`, about 2x44px), using icon-only segments on phones, and let the brand/project name be the part that shrinks. In the phone layout, move workspace switching into the bottom tab bar (see the phone shell in the architecture notes).

findings.problem: The design toolbar is about 2094px wide and scrolls sideways with no affordance. At MacBook widths the Arrange grid, Snap/View, Commands and the Properties panel toggle are off-screen. On a phone in the Laser workspace, the Machine drawer toggle is off-screen too.
findings.evidence: `.toolbar { overflow-x: auto }` (styles.css:797). At 1280x720: scrollWidth 2094 vs clientWidth 1280, and the horizontal scrollbar adds 11px of height (91 vs 80). The right panel toggle is the last child after `.tool-spacer` (Toolbar.tsx:213), so it is the first thing pushed off-screen. Group widths: 64, 77, 275, 143, 209, 212, 146, 143, 60, 209, 228 (Arrange), 129 (Snap/View), 85 (Commands), 64. In the Laser workspace at 375px the Machine toggle sits at x=466–530.
findings.recommendation: (a) Take both panel toggles out of the scrolling strip into fixed end caps (`.toolbar-start`, `.toolbar-end`, flex:none). (b) Add a `useRibbonOverflow()` ResizeObserver hook. Each `.tool-group` gets a priority and a group label, and when space runs out the lowest-priority groups collapse into one Fusion-style dropdown button ('CREATE ▾', 'MODIFY ▾', 'ARRANGE ▾'). EditMenus.tsx already has the dropdown pattern to reuse. (c) In compact mode with a fine pointer, show icons only with labels in tooltips (`.tool-btn span {display:none}`): buttons go from 64x52 to about 36x36 and the toolbar from 80px to about 44px tall.

findings.problem: On a 1280x720 browser area, chrome takes 377px of height, leaving the canvas 343px. That is 48% of the height and about 26% of the window area.
findings.evidence: Measured rows: topbar 48, doc-tabs row 31 (one tab open), toolbar 91, numeric bar 96, palette 29, timeline 58, status 24. Canvas stage: 688x343.
findings.recommendation:
Compact-mode target is about 176px of chrome:
- topbar 40, with doc tabs merged into it and the separate row (`.doc-tabs-row`) rendered only when two or more tabs are open
- toolbar 44 (icon-only)
- numeric bar 32 on a single row (see L5), or inline on the toolbar's right on wide screens
- palette 24
- timeline and status merged into one 32px row that expands to the full 58px strip on hover, tap or pin
That raises the canvas height from 343 to about 544px (+59%). Gate it on `data-layout=compact` and on `@media (max-height: 860px)`, so short MacBook windows get it even when they are wide.

findings.problem: A spacer element plus flex-wrap makes the numeric bar wrap onto an extra row, so it is 96px tall where 38px would do. On a phone it is 135px.
findings.evidence: workspace.css:515 `.numeric-sep { flex: 1 }` inside `.numeric-bar { flex-wrap: wrap }`. At 688px the three groups (231+302+102px plus gaps) nearly fill row 1. The 1px spacer wraps to row 2 and grows to the full width, which pushes the unit toggle (68px) to row 3 (measured tops 173, 195, 220).

architecture_notes:
CURRENT SHELL MAP (code)
- `.app` grid (styles.css:294): rows `48px | auto (doc tabs) | auto (toolbar) | minmax(0,1fr) (main) | auto (timeline, fixed 58px) | auto (status 24px)`. It uses `height: 100dvh`, left/right safe-area padding and `overflow: hidden`.
- **Main row:** `.main` is a flex row: `aside.panel-left` (272px) | `section.center` (flex column: NumericBar in Design → `.center-stage` with Viewport and PreviewTimeline → DockAreaHost bottom (max 38vh) → PaletteBar) | `aside.panel-right` (320px).
- **Panels:** each panel body hosts `DockAreaHost` plus `Dock` windows that portal into slots (Dock.tsx, DockHost.tsx, layout.ts with areas left/right/bottom/float, tab groups, float rects, visibility; persisted in localStorage). Collapsing a dock is a pref.
- **Floating windows:** FloatHost uses a fixed layer at z60.
- **Breakpoints:** JS `NARROW_QUERY (max-width:1023px)` adds `.narrow`, which turns panels into translateX drawers with a scrim (z20/15) and starts them closed. CSS breakpoints at 900/760/640/600/560/480 only hide text or turn grids into one column. The numeric bar uses `@container numbar`.
- **Tokens:** a complete colour token set, with dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme` plus `[data-theme]`; usePrefs sets `--ui-scale`, `--icon-scale` and `--handle-scale` inline. No space, size or z scales.
- **Dependencies:** react and react-dom only.

TARGET ARCHITECTURE
1. **Layout mode hook** (`workspace/layoutMode.ts`). One external store, like prefs.ts, built from matchMedia:
   - phone: `(max-width: 599px)`, or `(max-width: 899px) and (pointer: coarse) and (orientation: portrait)`
   - tablet: `(max-width: 1179px)`, or `(pointer: coarse)` without a fine `any-pointer`
   - compact: `(max-width: 1599px)` or `(max-height: 860px)`
   - wide: everything else
   It writes `data-layout`, `data-pointer` and `data-density` on `<html>`. Preferences can override it (Auto / Comfortable / Compact / Touch). App replaces `narrow` with `mode !== 'wide' && mode !== 'compact'` for drawer behaviour. Pure functions mean `npm test` can cover the mode resolution.
2. **Tokens** (`tokens.css`): size, space, z-index and bar-height scales, re-declared under `[data-density=compact]` and `[data-pointer=coarse]`. Every component CSS file moves to them over time, without a rewrite. Colour tokens stay as they are.
3. **Ribbon overflow** (`useRibbonOverflow`): each Toolbar group declares `{id, label, priority}`. A ResizeObserver measures and collapses groups from the lowest priority into Fusion-style 'GROUP ▾' dropdowns built from the EditMenus menu component. The panel toggles and the Laser group's Frame / Start / Stop frame are pinned and never collapse. Compact plus a fine pointer means icon-only buttons.
4. **Docks:**
   - Layout gets `sizes` and `areaMode` (pinned / rail / hidden), sanitised like the rest.
   - Splitters use pointer events with `touch-action: none`, plus double-click to reset.
   - Rail mode is a 32px strip of vertical titles; a tap or hover opens the area as an overlay at z20.
   - Auto policy: keep the canvas at least 640px wide, collapsing left first, then right.
   - Presets Wide / Compact / Touch go in the Window menu.
5. **Bottom chrome:** in compact mode, Timeline and StatusBar share one 32px row: timeline chips scroll, status cells sit on the right. A pin or chevron expands it to the full 58px Fusion strip. Doc tabs show only when two or more are open. The palette is 24px.
6. **Full screen:** the manifest and metas, a Full screen toggle (Fullscreen API, hidden when unsupported), and a Focus-canvas hotkey. Note the http limits: no install prompt or Window Controls Overlay without HTTPS. 'Open as window' / 'Add to Dock' / 'Add to Home Screen' still give an app-like window. If a true install matters, the Pi engine could later serve HTTPS with a locally trusted cert, which is a separate decision.
7. **Tablet layout** (iPad):
   - 44px tap targets.
   - The toolbar becomes a vertical tool rail on the canvas's left edge (select, rect, ellipse, text, pen, import, plus an Arrange popover). This frees the horizontal toolbar row, which keeps only the group dropdowns, Frame and Start.
   - The right area docks in landscape and becomes a drawer in portrait. The left Browser is always a rail or overlay.
   - Selection never auto-opens a drawer; a floating Properties pill does that on request.
   - Long-press opens the context menu (already pointer-based).
   - Keep LightBurn modifiers through an on-canvas modifier chip (Shift / Ctrl latch), because iPad has no keyboard by default.
8. **Phone layout:** a separate `PhoneShell` chosen in App when the mode is phone. It reuses Viewport, LaserDock, CutsLayers, PropertiesPanel, RunsCard and PreviewStatsCard.
   - **Top bar:** File/menu, project name, connection dot, STOP (always visible, fixed width).
   - **Body:** full-bleed canvas with fit/zoom overlay.
   - **Bottom tab bar** (safe-area aware): Canvas / Layers / Job / More. Each tab opens a bottom sheet (peek or full).
   - **On a phone:** job monitoring (progress, time, pause/resume, run history), framing and stop frame, Start or Request run (still gated by the app's approval / foot switch), layer power/speed/passes, select and move with X/Y/W/H, centre on stock or field, rotate 90, delete, import a file, simple text.
   - **Not on a phone:** node editing, pen and polygon, trim/weld, the docking tool, the art library editor, device editing, the lens wizard, G-code console. Leave them reachable via More → 'Desktop features' with a hint.
   - The timeline becomes a sheet listing steps; undo/redo sit in the sheet header.
9. **Dialogs:** full-screen sheets at 600px and below, a modal stack so Escape closes only the top one, and backdrop dismissal by click rather than pointerdown.

INCREMENTAL PLAN (each step is a small PR, no UI library)
- **Phase 0 (CSS fixes, about a day):** L1 STOP never clipped, L2 switcher floor, L3a panel toggles out of the scroller, L5 numeric-bar spacer, L11 safe-area row, L14 doc-tabs row only with two or more tabs.
- **Phase 1:** layoutMode hook plus tokens.css (z, space, size, density). Replace `.narrow` and `--tap` with the new tokens, and add the density preference.
- **Phase 2:** ribbon overflow and icon-only compact toolbar, merged timeline and status row, dock splitters with persisted sizes, rail mode, layout presets (L3, L4, L6, L10).
- **Phase 3:** manifest, metas and icons, Full screen toggle, Focus mode (L7).
- **Phase 4:** tablet. Coarse density, tool rail, selection pill instead of auto-opening drawers, inert drawers, float re-clamp (L8, L9, L15).
- **Phase 5:** PhoneShell with bottom tabs and sheets, and full-screen dialogs (L12).
- **Later:** migrate the remaining CSS to tokens and dedupe the dark palette (L13).

DEPENDENCY VERDICT: none needed. Splitters, ResizeObserver overflow, bottom sheets and rails are each 50–150 lines with the existing pointer utilities (pointer.ts, capturePointer). The only one worth considering later is `@floating-ui/dom` (MIT, about 10KB), if popovers and menus keep clipping at screen edges. Today ContextMenu clamps by hand and `.menu` is absolutely positioned with no flip. Avoid Radix, MUI and similar: too big, and they would fight the hand-built token theme.

EVIDENCE NOTE: all measurements were taken by viewport emulation in the built-in browser against the simulator at http://127.0.0.1:7979, at 1280x720, 1180x820, 1024x700 and 375x812. That covers Design and Laser in each, except Laser at 1180x820 and 1024x700, which I didn't measure. I only switched workspaces and read layout metrics; nothing was edited, burned or stopped. The viewport emulation was reset to desktop afterwards.

summary:
Input/touch audit (code only, read-only). The basics are in good shape. The canvas uses Pointer Events throughout, with touch-action:none and user-select:none on the viewport SVGs. A non-passive wheel listener is in place, two-finger pan/pinch is coalesced to animation frames, and capturePointer() exists. Menu items are 44px, .field-input inputs go to 16px on coarse pointers (no iOS focus zoom), and the node and line tools expose their key actions as buttons in the options bar.

The editing model is still mouse-and-keyboard only, though, and in some cases that is a real break on iPad, iPhone and MacBook:

1. **Touch has no LightBurn selection model.** One finger on empty space always pans, so there is no marquee and no crossing selection. Touch events carry no modifiers, so selection is always "replace". Select All, Invert, Copy, Cut, Paste and Paste in place can only be reached by keyboard or right-click. iOS never fires contextmenu, so the canvas, Browser, Layers and Timeline context menus cannot be opened at all.
2. **Shift/Ctrl/Alt drag behaviours have no touch path.** This covers constrain, snap off, guides only, draw from centre, rotate steps and node Shift-select.
3. **Some canvas tools act on pointerdown.** On touch, a finger that starts a pinch adds a stray line vertex, sets a measure point, completes a point pick, or runs Trim on the shape under it (with no hover preview first).
4. **Hit targets and slop are mouse-sized on every pointer.** Click tolerance is 5px, tap slop 4px, node tolerance 7px, scale-handle hit 16px and guide hit 9px. Nothing uses @media (pointer: coarse), so a finger tap on a selected object can become a tiny move.
5. **MacBook problems.**
   - A purely vertical two-finger scroll zooms, while any sideways component pans, so the mode flips mid-swipe.
   - There is no Space+drag pan and no middle button on a trackpad.
   - Safari's trackpad pinch (GestureEvents) is not handled. I believe this means Safari zooms the whole page; this needs checking on the machine.
   - Ctrl+click on a Mac fires contextmenu, which undoes a Ctrl-toggle selection.
6. **Timeline right-click menu is not kept on screen.** It is not clamped to the window and opens off-screen at the bottom bar, so Delete step is unreachable. The history marker is an 8px-wide drag target.
7. **Phone typing problems.**
   - Signed number fields use inputMode=decimal, so the iPhone keypad has no minus sign or maths operators. Negative X/Y positions are common because the field is centred on the origin.
   - Several inputs outside .field-input, and the on-canvas text editor, are under 16px, so iOS zooms the page when they get focus.
8. **Smaller items.**
   - No touch-action:manipulation or -webkit-touch-callout on the app chrome.
   - :hover styles stay highlighted after a tap on touch screens.
   - Some actions are double-click-only, and reordering uses HTML5 drag-and-drop, which is unreliable on touch.
   - Many controls are 18–28px.
   - There is no palm rejection when using an Apple Pencil.
   - Ruler guide drags depend on pointer capture having succeeded.

The architecture notes below propose a touch model that maps one finger to the left mouse button and two fingers to view navigation. It adds long-press for context menus, a latching modifier bar, a floating selection action bar, touch-sized tolerances chosen per event, commit-on-lift for canvas tools, and palm rejection. This keeps the LightBurn mouse behaviour exactly as it is.

findings.problem: Touch has no marquee, no crossing (right-to-left) marquee, and no add, toggle or remove selection. One finger on empty space always pans. Touch PointerEvents carry no modifier keys, so selectOpFor() always returns 'replace'. Selecting several objects on an iPad or phone is impossible except one at a time through the Browser tree, and Shift-click there does not work on touch either.
findings.evidence: Viewport.tsx:604-608 `if (e.pointerType === "touch") { gesture.current = { kind: "pan", ... clearOnTap } ; return; }` happens before the marquee branch at 609. modsOf (484-488) reads only e.shiftKey, ctrlKey, metaKey and altKey, and selection.ts:47 selectOpFor maps those to the op. BrowserPanel.tsx:233 and CutsLayers.tsx:289 rely on e.shiftKey and e.ctrlKey for multi-select.
findings.recommendation: Make one finger behave like the left mouse button and two fingers handle view navigation. One-finger drag on empty space draws the same marquee as the mouse (left to right encloses, right to left crosses, same solid and dashed styles). Pan and pinch stay on two fingers, which already works through the pinch branch (504-509, 721-731). Feed a virtual-modifier store (the modifier bar in T3) into modsOf() so Add, Toggle and Remove work for taps and marquees. Offer the old 'one finger pans' behaviour as a preference for phone users if wanted.

findings.problem: iOS Safari does not fire contextmenu on long-press, and the app has no long-press of its own, so every right-click menu is unreachable on iPad and iPhone. On the canvas that leaves Cut, Copy, Paste, Paste in place, Select All, Invert Selection, docking and the text, file and design context items with no touch path. Copy and Paste exist only as keyboard shortcuts and in this menu. The same applies to the Browser layer and object menus, the CutsLayers layer menu (including Flash layer), Timeline step menu, PagesDock, ArtLibrary, MaterialLibrary and DockHost tab menus.
findings.evidence: Viewport.tsx:1077-1084 opens the menu only from onContextMenu. App.tsx:950-982 builds menuItems (Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Invert) used only by that menu. The only other Select All path is the Ctrl+A key at App.tsx:763. Grep finds no long-press or timer-based press anywhere in web/src.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared long-press helper (pointer.ts, pure and testable): 500 ms with less than 8 px of movement and no second pointer. It cancels the pending gesture and calls the same onContextMenu(x, y), selecting the object under the finger first as right-click does. Use it on the canvas, tree and table rows, timeline chips, art and library items. Also add a floating selection action bar on touch (see architecture notes) with Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Group and a ⋯ button that opens the full context menu, so the menu is discoverable without knowing about long-press.

findings.problem: Every LightBurn modifier behaviour needs a physical key. Shift constrains moves, nodes and line angles and squares rect/ellipse. Ctrl turns snapping off, draws from the centre, scales about the centre and gives 5° rotation steps. Alt snaps to guides only. Shift frees the aspect ratio when scaling and gives 15° rotation steps, and Shift-click selects nodes. Touch, Apple Pencil and an iPad without a keyboard have none of these.
findings.evidence: Viewport.tsx:636-645 (move: m.shift → constrainDelta), 386-405 (snapOpts reads m.ctrl and m.alt), 418-424 (drawEnd: Ctrl draws from centre, Shift squares), 671 scaleFromHandle(..., m), 682 rotateFromHandle(..., m); EditTools.tsx:579 clickNode(..., m.shift). pointer.ts modifierReplay re-evaluates a drag when a key changes, so the plumbing for live toggles already exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a modifier bar on coarse pointers, a floating pill at the canvas's bottom-left. Its toggles change with the tool. Select: Add, Toggle, Constrain, No snap. Rect/Ellipse/Circle: Square, From centre, No snap. Rotating: Fine steps. Node: Add to node selection. A tap latches the toggle for the next gesture and a double-tap locks it, with a clear lit state. Merge it in modsOf() as physical OR virtual, and when a toggle changes mid-drag call update(lastMove.s, mods), the same path modifierReplay uses. Show the active toggles in the bottom-left readout.

findings.problem: The line, measure, pick and trim tools act on the first pointerdown. On touch, a pinch always starts with one finger, so the first finger's down has already happened when the second arrives. The Viewport then calls ext.cancel(), but cancel() only pops the point for the Pen tool. A Line vertex, a measure start point or a completed pick stays. Trim runs immediately on the down with no preview, because the trim-hover highlight needs hover. Starting a pinch over a shape in Trim mode cuts it.
findings.evidence: EditTools.tsx:588-609 (line/pen: `store.set({ pen: [...pts, { p: q }] })` on down; line leaves gest 'none'), 852-861 cancel() pops only `if (g.kind === "pen")`, 610-626 measure sets meas on down, 640-662 trim executes G.trim on down, 663-677 pick finishes the pick on down. Viewport.tsx:504-509 cancels on the second finger.
findings.recommendation: For touch (and optionally pen), defer the commit to lift. down() records a pending press. If a second pointer arrives, or the press moves past the drag slop into a drag, the pending press is dropped. A clean lift commits. For Trim on touch, show et-trim-hover while the finger is down and remove the piece on lift. Lifting with the finger moved away, or a second finger, cancels. At minimum make cancel() roll back whatever this gesture added: the line point, the measure start and the pick point.

findings.problem: All canvas tolerances are mouse-sized and the same for every pointer type, and nothing in CSS or JS uses (pointer: coarse). The handle size preference defaults to 1×. A finger (about 7-10 mm) cannot reliably hit a 1.3px outline with a 5px tolerance, a 16px handle or a 9px guide. The 4px tap slop means normal finger jitter on a selected object becomes a move: a tap commits a tiny object.transform and an undo step.

architecture_notes:
Proposed touch interaction model. It keeps the LightBurn mouse behaviour exactly as it is today and makes touch a faithful translation of it. "One finger is the left mouse button, two fingers are the view."

1) Input classification (pointer.ts, pure, unit-tested like pointer.test.ts)
- `pointerClass(e)` returns mouse, pen or touch, and `TOL[class]` gives the tolerances:

  | Pointer | Click | Slop | Node | Snap | Handle hit | Double-tap | Long-press |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Mouse | 5 | 4 | 7 | 8 | 16 | 6px / 350ms | – |
  | Pen | 8 | 6 | 10 | 10 | 24 | – | – |
  | Touch | 14 | 10 | 18 | 14 | 44 | 24px / 400ms | 500ms |

- Pass the class in PointerInfo and CanvasCtx (`ctx.tol`) so EditTools, Viewport and snapping all use one source. Decide per event, not per device: an iPad with a trackpad gets mouse tolerances.
- A `virtualMods` external store (useSyncExternalStore) holds the modifier-bar state. `modsOf(e)` becomes physical OR virtual (Mac: metaKey stands for Ctrl, see T7). A toggle change during a drag reuses the existing modifierReplay → `update(lastMove.s, m)` path.

2) Gesture arbiter (Viewport onPointerDown, onPointerMove, endPointer)
- **First touch:** start a *pending* gesture. Select/move, marquee, draw, handle and canvas-tool behave exactly as for the mouse, but nothing is committed or added on down. Canvas tools get `down` only once the press is known to be a tap (lift within slop) or a drag (past slop).
- **Second touch:** if it arrives before slop or within about 150 ms, the pending gesture is dropped without side effects and becomes pan + pinch, using the existing pinch code. If it arrives mid-drag, it cancels the drag (the touch "Esc").
- **Long-press:** 500 ms within slop and no second finger opens the context menu at the finger, using the same handler as right-click and selecting the hit first if it is not selected. Show a short ring animation so the user sees it coming.
- **Pen palm rejection:** while a pen is active, touches only navigate.
- **Optional, Procreate-style:** two-finger tap = undo, three-finger tap = redo. These are cheap and natural for Fusion and LightBurn users on an iPad.

3) Select-tool semantics on touch (mirroring LightBurn)
- **Tap an object:** select it (replace). With Add latched, add it; with Toggle latched, toggle it.
- **Tap an already-selected object again:** toggle between scale handles and rotate handles. This is LightBurn's click-again rotate mode, and it avoids overlapping 44px hit areas on small parts.
- **Drag an object:** select and move it. Constrain latched = Shift (H/V/45°); No-snap latched = Ctrl.
- **One-finger drag on empty space:** marquee. Left to right encloses (solid); right to left crosses (dashed green, same styles as now). The Add/Toggle latches apply.
- **Tap empty space:** clear the selection (as now).
- **Two fingers:** always pan and pinch. A double-tap with two fingers fits the field.
- **Handles:** about 2× visual size and 44px hit areas when the last pointer was touch, with the selection box padding scaled so handles do not cover the part.

4) Modifier bar (coarse pointers only, bottom-left over the canvas, one-hand reachable on a phone)
- Context-sensitive toggles:
  - Select: Add (⇧), Toggle (⌘/Ctrl), Constrain, No snap.
  - Rect/Ellipse: Square, From centre, No snap.
  - Circle: No snap.
  - Line/Pen: 15° steps.
  - While rotating: Fine steps (5°).
  - Node: Add-to-node-selection.
- A tap latches the toggle for the next gesture (auto-clears); a double-tap locks it until tapped again. The lit state also appears in the bottom-left readout.
- It is the same Mods object the keyboard produces, so EditTools and editing.ts need no new logic.

5) Selection action bar (touch; also useful on a MacBook)
- A floating pill above the selection bounds, or docked above the timeline on a phone, with Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Group/Ungroup, Rotate 90, Flip and ⋯ (opens the existing App menuItems ContextMenu).
- This makes Select All, Invert, Paste in place and Docking reachable without long-press discovery.
- Add a nudge pad to the Properties panel's position section on coarse pointers.

6) Canvas tools on touch
- Place on lift. Pressing shows the snap glyph and readout in a bubble about 60px above the finger, dragging adjusts, and lifting commits.
- The line and pen bar gains "Undo point". The existing Finish and Close buttons stay.
- Trim highlights the piece while the finger is down and removes it on lift.
- The node bar gains "Insert node". Node marquee is a one-finger drag on empty space (already the case).

7) Desktop and trackpad
- Space+drag pan and Shift+wheel horizontal pan.
- Wheel streams are latched to pan or zoom per gesture.
- A "Trackpad: scroll pans, pinch zooms" preference (on by default on Mac).
- Safari gesturestart/gesturechange handled with preventDefault.
- Cmd mapping on Mac, and Ctrl+click left as the Mac right-click.

8) Global CSS for touch
- `html{touch-action:manipulation}`.
- `.app{user-select:none;-webkit-touch-callout:none}`, re-enabled for input, textarea and contenteditable.
- `@media (hover:hover)` around hover visuals, plus :active feedback.
- `@media (pointer:coarse)`: inputs ≥16px, dense controls ≥40-44px (mini-grid, doc tabs, et-bar, c-order, float grip), and the timeline marker hit area ≥32px.

Implementation order (each step independently testable)
1. Tolerance table and per-event classes. This removes accidental micro-moves.
2. Deferred commit and long-press in the arbiter. This fixes the stray points and Trim-on-pinch, and gives context menus on iOS.
3. Touch marquee and the modifier bar.
4. Selection action bar and nudge pad.
5. Trackpad, Space pan and Safari gestures.
6. CSS coarse and hover pass.
7. Timeline popover and marker hit area.

Keep the arbiter as a pure state machine in pointer.ts (inputs: down, move and up events with class, time and position; outputs: tap, drag, pinch, long-press, cancel) so `npm test` covers it without a DOM.
