Nothing was edited, and nothing was run against the engine, port 7878 or the Pi.

summary:
Full screen / app-window audit of OpenEtch (code read-only, plus platform research). Today the app has none of the pieces it needs to run as an app window. There is no in-app full screen toggle and no shortcut for it (F11 is listed as reserved for the browser in hotkeys.ts). There is no web app manifest, no icons or favicon, no theme-color and no service worker. index.html has only a viewport tag with viewport-fit=cover and the old apple-mobile-web-app-capable tag.

Plain http from the Pi's LAN IP still allows a lot. The Fullscreen API does not need a secure context. It works over http in Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Windows and macOS), in Safari on macOS 16.4+ and in Safari on iPad (with caveats). Safari 17+ on macOS Sonoma can "Add to Dock" any site, and iOS/iPadOS can open any site added to the Home Screen as a standalone web app (the default for every site since iOS 26), both over http.

Plain http blocks other things: installing the app in Chrome/Edge/Android (manifest-based), window-controls-overlay, service workers, Screen Wake Lock, Keyboard Lock and the browser camera (getUserMedia). The app's Camera panel already says so. On http the browser also sends no Sec-Fetch-Site header for click approval. iPhone Safari still has no element fullscreen, so on the phone the Home Screen web app is the only "full screen" route.

Two problems in the engine and app would break installed app windows even with HTTPS:
- The bearer token is kept in localStorage. Safari's Dock apps get only a copy of the cookies, and iOS Home Screen apps have their own storage, so neither sees the token.
- The token is generated again on every engine restart unless --token is passed, and the UI has no screen for entering a token after a 401.

The static file server also needs work: there are no Cache-Control headers and no compression (the main JS bundle is 1.15 MB uncompressed). A missing /assets/* file, favicon.ico or manifest is answered with index.html and a 200 status, so a stale cached index.html after an update can leave a blank page.

On the layout side:
- The bottom safe-area inset is applied to the timeline, but the status bar is the last row, so on iPad and iPhone it sits under the home indicator.
- There is no handling of the top inset.
- Ctrl+wheel or a trackpad pinch over the side panels zooms the whole page. On iPad, pinch and double-tap over the panels do the same.

Recommended order:
1. A full screen toggle: a button in the top bar, a View/command palette entry, and a rebindable Alt+Enter shortcut. Use the Fullscreen API on documentElement, sync state from fullscreenchange, and take keyboard lock for Esc in Chromium where available.
2. A manifest with display_override window-controls-overlay then standalone, plus icons, an apple-touch-icon, theme-color and the iOS meta tags.
3. A persistent token in the config dir and a "Connect to engine" screen.
4. Safe-area and zoom fixes.
5. Engine static serving: Cache-Control, precompressed gzip/br files, and a 404 for missing assets.
6. An HTTPS path. Short term with no code: `tailscale serve` (a publicly trusted *.ts.net certificate, but every device needs the Tailscale app) or Caddy with `tls internal` (needs its root CA installed on each device). Long term: an engine `--tls-cert/--tls-key` option, optionally with a built-in local CA and a one-tap profile download.

For the owner's own Windows PC and MacBook in Chrome/Edge, a zero-infrastructure stopgap is the flag "Insecure origins treated as secure" (chrome://flags or edge://flags) set to http://192.168.1.20:7878. This makes manifest install and window-controls-overlay work over http.

findings.problem: There is no in-app full screen control or shortcut. On a 1280x800-1470x956 MacBook, browser chrome (tabs, address bar, macOS menu bar) takes 120-180 px of height away from the canvas. The owner has no app-like way to reclaim it, and F11 is a browser-only mode the app cannot see or exit.
findings.evidence: A grep of web/src for requestFullscreen, fullscreenElement or fullscreenchange finds nothing. web/src/workspace/hotkeys.ts:183 lists F11 in RESERVED ('Chords a browser keeps for itself'). TopBar.tsx has no such button. index.html has only viewport and apple-mobile-web-app-capable meta tags.
findings.recommendation:
Add a 'Full screen' action (an id like view.fullscreen) in three places: an icon button in the top bar's .topbar-actions, a View/command palette entry, and a rebindable default shortcut of Alt+Enter (Option+Return on Mac). Alt+Enter is unbound and not taken by any browser. Do not use F11: browsers keep it for their own full screen, and the page cannot intercept it reliably. Do not use Cmd+Shift+F either, which Chrome on Mac uses for 'always show toolbar in full screen'.

Implementation:
- Call `document.documentElement.requestFullscreen({navigationUI:'hide'})`, falling back to webkitRequestFullscreen for older Safari. Exit with document.exitFullscreen or webkitExitFullscreen.
- Call it directly in the click or keydown handler, because it needs transient user activation. The keymap's capture listener counts as activation, since keydown is an activation event.
- Show the button only when `document.fullscreenEnabled || document.webkitFullscreenEnabled`. That is false on iPhone Safari and in iOS Home Screen apps; in that case show 'Install as app' (see FS-09) instead.
- Track state from the fullscreenchange/webkitfullscreenchange events plus `matchMedia('(display-mode: fullscreen)')`. Chromium also matches that query in its own F11 mode, so the icon can show 'Exit full screen' and tell the user to press F11 when the browser, not the page, owns full screen.
- The Fullscreen API needs no secure context, so this works today over http://192.168.1.20:7878 in Chrome, Edge and Firefox on Windows and macOS, and in Safari on macOS (unprefixed since 16.4).
- iPadOS Safari supports it with caveats: an X overlay, a swipe-down exit, and focusing a text field or showing the on-screen keyboard has been reported to drop out of full screen. On iPad, prefer the Home Screen web app and treat the toggle as a bonus.
- Remember the user's choice only as a hint ('re-enter full screen?' toast after a reload). Browsers do not allow entering full screen on load.

findings.problem: There is no web app manifest, no icons (not even a favicon), no theme-color and no Apple touch icon. In Chrome or Edge the app cannot become an installed window with its own Dock or taskbar icon and only a title bar, and window-controls-overlay (a Fusion-like look with the top bar in the title bar) is impossible. Safari 'Add to Dock' and iOS/iPadOS 'Add to Home Screen' produce a generic or screenshot icon titled from the page.
findings.evidence: web/index.html contains only charset, viewport (width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover), apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes and the title. web/public does not exist. web/dist holds only index.html, assets/ and parity. curl -I http://127.0.0.1:7979/manifest.webmanifest and /favicon.ico both return 200 text/html (the index.html fallback). The only brand mark is a CSS gradient square (styles.css:328-334).
findings.recommendation:
Add web/public/manifest.webmanifest (Vite copies public/ to dist):
- name 'OpenEtch', short_name 'OpenEtch', id '/', start_url '/', scope '/'
- display 'standalone' and display_override ['window-controls-overlay','standalone','minimal-ui']
- background_color and theme_color set to the dark chrome colour (#23262a), orientation 'any'
- icons: 192 and 512 PNG, a 512 maskable PNG and an SVG; optional shortcuts such as 'New document'

Add to web/index.html:
- `<link rel=manifest href=/manifest.webmanifest>` and `<link rel=icon href=/icon.svg type=image/svg+xml>`, plus a favicon.ico or 32px PNG
- `<link rel=apple-touch-icon href=/apple-touch-icon.png>` (180x180, opaque)
- `<meta name=theme-color>` twice, with media='(prefers-color-scheme: light)' and '(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'
- `<meta name=color-scheme content='light dark'>`
- `<meta name=mobile-web-app-capable content=yes>`; keep the apple- one, since Chrome now warns that it alone is deprecated
- `<meta name=apple-mobile-web-app-title content=OpenEtch>`
- `<meta name=apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style content=black-translucent>`, only together with the top safe-area padding in FS-05

Design a real icon from the orange/blue brand mark.

For window-controls-overlay, give .topbar these CSS rules when `(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)` matches: padding-left env(titlebar-area-x, 0), width/height from env(titlebar-area-width/height), app-region: drag (and -webkit-app-region) on the empty top bar background, and app-region: no-drag on every button, menu and input. The macOS traffic lights and the Windows min/max/close buttons then share the 48 px top bar, as in Fusion 360.

On plain http, Chrome and Edge ignore the manifest for installation, so this pays off fully only with FS-04. Safari's Dock apps and iOS Home Screen apps use the icons, name and status bar meta tags over http too.

findings.area: Auth token vs installed app windows
findings.problem:
Installed app windows on Apple platforms will open logged out, and the app has no way to recover:
- The bearer token lives only in localStorage ('openetch.token') and is removed from the URL on first load.
- Safari 'Add to Dock' apps get a copy of Safari's cookies, not its localStorage.
- iOS/iPadOS Home Screen web apps have storage separate from Safari.
- The saved start URL no longer contains ?token=.
- The engine generates a new random token on every start when it listens off loopback without --token. That is the systemd example in ARCHITECTURE.md (`--listen 0.0.0.0:7878`), so every Pi restart or update also silently invalidates the token on every browser, Dock app and Home Screen app.
- The UI has no 401 handling and no screen for entering a token.
findings.evidence: web/src/api/client.ts:16-44: initAuthToken reads ?token=, stores it in localStorage, then history.replaceState removes it. crates/engine/src/main.rs:208-213: `(None, false) => Some(generate_token()?)`. ARCHITECTURE.md:38: ExecStart has no --token. A grep for 401 or Unauthorized in web/src outside tests finds nothing. security.rs:189 answers 401 with 'open the URL the engine printed at startup', which is printed to the Pi's journal, which the owner cannot see from an iPad.
findings.recommendation:
Engine side: generate the token once and keep it in <config-dir>/access-token (mode 0600), reusing it across restarts. Add a command like `openetch token [--rotate]` (similar to set-pin) that prints it and a pairing URL. Optionally render that URL as a QR code in the terminal.

Web side: when /api/* answers 401, or no token is stored, show a full-page 'Connect to OpenEtch' card. It should have a token field (paste), 'Remember on this device', a short explanation of where to find the token (ssh to the Pi, then `openetch token`), and later a 'Scan QR' option (camera needs HTTPS). Store the token in localStorage as now.

Optional: at the moment the engine accepts ?token=, also set an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure-when-https cookie, and accept it in the guard as an alternative to the bearer header. Safari's 'Add to Dock' copies cookies into the new app, so it would arrive already logged in. The existing Origin check still guards against CSRF.

Do not put the token in the manifest's start_url.
findings.viewport: Safari Dock app (macOS), iPad/iPhone Home Screen app

findings.area: Secure context / HTTPS on the Pi
findings.problem:
The production URL http://192.168.1.20:7878 is not a secure context. In Chromium, Firefox and Safari that blocks:
- Chrome/Edge/Android Chrome manifest install, and with it window-controls-overlay and the standalone app window
- service workers
- Screen Wake Lock (keeping the iPad or phone screen on while watching a burn)
- Keyboard Lock (Esc in full screen, FS-07)
- getUserMedia, so the app's own 'browser camera' button is disabled
- Sec-Fetch-Site on the click-approval request, which the engine docs already note leaves only the Origin check
- in Chromium, also the async Clipboard API and Web Share

The engine has no TLS of its own (updates.rs says it carries no TLS stack).
findings.evidence: web/src/libs/Camera.tsx:452 `can = !!navigator.mediaDevices?.getUserMedia`. The locale string cam.noBrowserCam reads 'needs https or localhost'. security.rs:61-64 documents that there is no Sec-Fetch-Site on plain http. tower-http features are only fs and cors (Cargo.toml:51). The client is already HTTPS-ready: api/client.ts:272 picks wss: when the page is https.
findings.recommendation:
Offer HTTPS as an option and keep http working. The realistic options for a Pi on a home LAN:

(a) Tailscale. `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:7878` gives a publicly trusted Let's Encrypt certificate for pi.<tailnet>.ts.net, renewed automatically, with nothing to install in any trust store. Every device needs the Tailscale app running: macOS, Windows, iPadOS, iOS and Android all have one, and it uses the VPN slot on iOS. LAN traffic still goes direct over WireGuard. It also gives remote access, which is acceptable because burns only start from Start or the foot switch. Zero engine code. This is the best short-term option.

(b) Caddy on the Pi with `tls internal`, giving a hostname such as openetch.local (avahi) and/or the IP. Caddy runs a local CA and renews certificates itself, and it proxies WebSocket, does HTTP/2, and compresses with gzip/zstd. The root CA must be installed once per device:
- macOS: Keychain, set to Always Trust
- Windows: Trusted Root store
- iOS/iPadOS: install the profile, then turn it on under Settings > General > About > Certificate Trust Settings
- Android: a user CA works in Chrome
- Firefox: uses OS roots by default on Windows and Mac

(c) mkcert. The same trust setup as (b), but certificates are issued by hand and expire after about 2 years. The certificate files would feed (b) or (e).

(d) A domain the owner owns plus a Let's Encrypt DNS-01 certificate (Caddy DNS plugin or certbot), with an A record pointing at 192.168.1.20. Publicly trusted, with no setup on devices. It costs a domain and a DNS API token, and some routers' DNS-rebind protection must allow the private answer.

(e) The engine serving TLS itself: `--tls-cert/--tls-key` (rustls through axum-server or tokio-rustls, with ring for easy aarch64 builds), plus an optional http listener that redirects to https. Optionally a built-in local CA (rcgen) that serves its root certificate and an iOS .mobileconfig at http://<pi>:7878/ca for one-tap install. This is the most integrated option and the most code.

Two caveats for any proxy setup:
- The engine currently decides whether a token is needed from its listen address. Behind a proxy it would listen on 127.0.0.1 and turn the token off while LAN clients reach it through Caddy or Tailscale. Require --token, or the persisted token from FS-03, whenever a proxy fronts the engine, and document it.
- Add the HTTPS hostname with --allow-host. The Origin same-host check already ignores scheme and port.

Do not use a plain self-signed certificate that users click through: Chromium then refuses service workers and installation, and iOS Home Screen apps will not load it.

Stopgap for the owner's own PC and Mac in Chrome/Edge with no infrastructure: set chrome://flags (or edge://flags) 'Insecure origins treated as secure' to http://192.168.1.20:7878. Manifest install, window-controls-overlay, wake lock and the camera then work over http in that browser profile.
findings.viewport: all remote devices (MacBook, PC, iPad, phone)

findings.area: Safe areas (home indicator, notch, standalone status bar)
findings.problem: The bottom safe-area inset is padded onto the timeline, but the status bar is the grid row below it. On an iPad with Face ID or an iPhone, the status bar (cursor XY and snap readout) therefore sits under the home indicator and the inset gap appears between the timeline and the status bar. There is no top inset handling. That is fine for a Safari tab or the default standalone status bar, but it breaks the moment black-translucent is used, and it ignores titlebar-area for window-controls-overlay.
findings.evidence: styles.css:1632-1637: `.timeline { height: calc(58px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) }`. App.tsx:1395 renders <Timeline> and App.tsx:1401 renders <StatusBar> after it. styles.css:295-302: `.app` has 100dvh, a grid-template-rows first row of a fixed 48px, and left/right safe-area padding only. workspace/workspace.css:530 .statusbar has no inset.
findings.recommendation:
Move the bottom inset to the last row: give `.statusbar` padding-bottom env(safe-area-inset-bottom) and min-height calc(24px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)), and remove it from `.timeline`. If the status bar is hidden on phones, apply the inset to whichever row is last. Simpler still: put `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` on `.app` and paint it with the status bar colour.

For the top, use `grid-template-rows: calc(48px + env(safe-area-inset-top)) ...` with `.topbar { padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top) }`. Together with apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent and theme-color, the iOS/iPadOS Home Screen app then draws its own top bar under the status bar, which looks more app-like.

Fixed and floating layers also need insets: toasts, drawers (.drawer-scrim), the context menu, the floating NumericBar and the bottom sheets on phones. Test the iPad in Slide Over and Stage Manager windows too.
findings.viewport: iPad (Face ID models), iPhone, Home Screen web app

findings.area: Accidental page zoom / bounce on touch and trackpad
findings.problem:
Only the canvas SVG intercepts wheel input and has touch-action:none. Over the side panels, timeline or top bar:
- a trackpad pinch or Ctrl+wheel in Chrome, Edge or Firefox zooms the whole UI (it stays zoomed for that origin)
- in Safari on macOS a pinch fires gesture events and zooms the page
- on iPad a two-finger pinch or a double-tap on a panel zooms the page, because iOS ignores user-scalable=no
- Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0 while a text field has focus fall through to browser zoom, because the keymap returns early when typing

The html/body/#root overscroll-behavior:none (styles.css:262) already prevents scroll bounce and pull-to-refresh.
findings.evidence: Viewport.tsx:323-336: a wheel listener with passive:false on svgRef only. styles.css:1318: `.viewport svg { touch-action: none }`. No global touch-action, and no gesturestart handler anywhere. useKeymap.ts:73: `if (typingIn(e.target) && chord !== 'F1') return;`
findings.recommendation:
- Add a window-level `wheel` listener ({passive:false}) that calls preventDefault when e.ctrlKey and the target is outside the canvas. Optionally route it to the canvas zoom.
- For Safari, add `gesturestart`, `gesturechange` and `gestureend` listeners on document that call preventDefault.
- Set `html { touch-action: manipulation }` and `touch-action: pan-x pan-y` on scrollable panels and lists. This kills double-tap zoom and pinch zoom on iPad while keeping panel scrolling. Keep touch-action:none on the canvas and on drag handles.
- In the keymap, always call preventDefault on Ctrl/Cmd plus =, - and 0, even while typing, so the UI never browser-zooms. The app's own --ui-scale preference is the supported way to scale the UI.
- Add `-webkit-touch-callout: none` to the canvas and toolbars, so a long press on iPad does not open the image or link callout.

findings.problem: The app uses Esc heavily (cancel the tool or the drawing, deselect, close dialogs; useKeymap lets Esc through to dialogs). In element full screen every browser takes Esc to exit full screen, so cancelling a pen path or a marquee also kicks the user out of full screen.
findings.evidence: useKeymap.ts:61 ('Escape still reaches the dialog's close handler'). No navigator.keyboard usage anywhere in web/src.
findings.recommendation: In Chromium (Chrome/Edge), after requestFullscreen succeeds, call `navigator.keyboard?.lock(['Escape'])`, or pass the new `keyboardLock` option of requestFullscreen where supported. Esc then reaches the app, and the user holds Esc to leave full screen (Chrome shows that hint). This needs a secure context (FS-04), and Safari and Firefox do not support it. Where it is unavailable, show a one-time tip on entering full screen ('Esc leaves full screen; use Alt+Enter to toggle') and offer the toolbar button to re-enter. An installed standalone app window avoids the conflict entirely, so promote it as the preferred 'title bar only' mode.

findings.area: Engine static file serving (MIME, caching, compression, fallback)
findings.problem: ServeDir has an SPA fallback to index.html for every unknown path, including /assets/*.js, /favicon.ico and a future /manifest.webmanifest or /sw.js, and answers them with 200 text/html. There is no Cache-Control on index.html or on the hashed assets, so browsers cache them heuristically from Last-Modified (Safari is aggressive). After an engine or web update, a cached index.html can request old hashed bundles. Those come back as HTML with a JS MIME expectation, and the page is blank until a hard reload. Installed app windows and iOS Home Screen apps have no reload button. There is also no compression: the 1,146,534-byte JS bundle and the 85 KB CSS go uncompressed over the Pi's Wi-Fi to phones and iPads.
findings.evidence: crates/engine/src/api.rs:86-88: `ServeDir::new(dir).fallback(ServeFile::new(dir.join("index.html")))`. curl -I on 127.0.0.1:7979: index.html is 'content-type: text/html', last-modified, no cache-control. assets/index-BOkRz1yM.js is 'text/javascript', content-length 1146534, no cache-control, no content-encoding even with Accept-Encoding: gzip, br. /favicon.ico and /manifest.webmanifest return 200 text/html. Cargo.toml:51: tower-http features [fs, cors]. MIME types are fine: mime_guess maps webmanifest to application/manifest+json.
findings.recommendation:
- Fall back to index.html only for navigations: GET requests whose path has no file extension and that do not start with /assets/, or with Accept: text/html. Answer 404 everywhere else.
- Add `Cache-Control: no-cache` on index.html, manifest.webmanifest and sw.js, and `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on /assets/* (the files are content-hashed).
- Precompress at build time (a vite compression plugin, or a small script writing .br and .gz next to each asset) and serve with `ServeDir::precompressed_br().precompressed_gzip()`, which costs no CPU on the Pi. Alternatively enable the tower-http `compression-br` and `compression-gzip` features with a CompressionLayer limited to static files.
- Consider not shipping sourcemaps to the Pi (vite.config.ts `sourcemap: true`), or exclude .map files from compression and caching.
- If HTTPS arrives, a small service worker can come later: network-first for index.html, cache-first for /assets/*, never /api or /mcp. It speeds up reopening the app and gives an 'engine unreachable' shell. With the caching headers above it is optional, and it must never serve a stale UI against a newer engine.
findings.viewport: all; worst on phone/iPad over Wi-Fi and in installed app windows

findings.problem: The way to get an app-like window differs on every device the owner uses, and nothing in the app explains it or detects the current mode. iPhone has no Fullscreen API at all, so the phone's only route to a full-screen app is Add to Home Screen.
findings.evidence: There is no display-mode detection (matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)') or navigator.standalone) anywhere in web/src, and no 'install' or 'beforeinstallprompt' handling.
findings.recommendation:
Add a 'Use as an app' item, for example in the Help menu and on first visit on touch devices, that detects the platform and display mode and shows the right steps:
- Chrome/Edge, once HTTPS or the flag is in place: an Install button driven by beforeinstallprompt, or the browser's Install app menu item
- Safari 17+ on macOS: File > Add to Dock (works over http)
- iPad and iPhone: Share > Add to Home Screen, with Open as Web App on (iOS/iPadOS 26 turns this on for every site; also works over http)
- Firefox on Windows: Taskbar Tabs (experimental, Firefox 143+)
- Android Chrome: Install app (needs HTTPS)

Hide the item when already standalone. In standalone mode, also hide the full screen button where document.fullscreenEnabled is false.

findings.problem: An installed app window or Dock app shows only document.title in its title bar, and that is always the static 'OpenEtch'. Fusion and LightBurn show the open document and an unsaved-changes marker.
findings.evidence: A grep for document.title in web/src finds nothing. index.html:7 has <title>OpenEtch</title>.
findings.recommendation: Keep document.title in sync as '<project or doc name>' + ' •' when dirty + ' — OpenEtch', using the projectName, docName and dirty values TopBar already receives. With window-controls-overlay this text is hidden, so the top bar's own ProjectIndicator carries it.

findings.problem: Context menus and some popovers cap their height with 100vh. In iPad and iPhone Safari tabs, 100vh is the large viewport (the toolbar collapsed), so menus near the bottom can extend under the Safari toolbar or the keyboard. The shell already uses 100dvh correctly.
findings.evidence: styles.css:1789 `.ctx-menu { max-height: calc(100vh - 8px) }`. components/edit.css:320 has the same rule.
findings.recommendation: Use `calc(100dvh - 8px - env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`, with a 100vh fallback declared first. For menus opened while the on-screen keyboard is up, consider sizing from visualViewport.

architecture_notes:
What each browser allows for OpenEtch served at http://192.168.1.20:7878. Researched in November 2026; behaviour on real iPad and iPhone hardware is not verified.

Element full screen (Fullscreen API on document.documentElement). Needs a user gesture. Does not need HTTPS.
- Chrome/Edge (Windows, macOS): yes. Esc exits; with HTTPS, Keyboard Lock can keep Esc for the app.
- Firefox: yes.
- Safari on macOS 16.4+: yes, unprefixed.
- iPadOS Safari: supported. Caveats: an X overlay, swipe down exits, and focusing an input or opening the keyboard has been reported to exit full screen.
- iPhone Safari: no, still video-only as of iOS 26. The WebKit bug and forum threads show no element full screen in iOS 26 or the Safari 27 betas.
- Android Chrome: yes.

App window with only a title bar:
- Chrome/Edge: manifest install with display standalone, or window-controls-overlay to merge the top bar into the title bar. Needs a secure context: HTTPS, localhost, or the 'Insecure origins treated as secure' flag for that exact origin. Chrome's 'Install page as app' / Create shortcut 'Open as window' may work on http without a manifest; not verified.
- Safari 17+ (macOS Sonoma or later): File > Add to Dock works for any site, http included. It copies cookies but not localStorage, which is why FS-03 matters, and it uses the manifest or apple- meta tags when present.
- iOS/iPadOS: Add to Home Screen. Since iOS/iPadOS 26 every site opens as a web app by default; works over http. Its storage is isolated from Safari. Without black-translucent it shows the status bar only.
- Firefox on Windows: Taskbar Tabs (experimental, Labs, 143+). Firefox on macOS: none.
- Android: real install needs HTTPS.

APIs that need HTTPS and matter for this app: service worker, beforeinstallprompt/installability (Chromium), Screen Wake Lock (keep the iPad awake while monitoring a burn), Keyboard Lock (Esc in full screen), getUserMedia (Camera.tsx browser camera), Sec-Fetch-* headers (strengthen click approval), async Clipboard (copy/paste currently uses copy/paste events, which work on http).

Engine changes to support all of this:
- Optional TLS: --tls-cert/--tls-key with rustls, or document Caddy / tailscale serve in front.
- A persistent access token, and a 'require token even on loopback' mode for proxy setups.
- --allow-host for the HTTPS name.
- Static serving: a real 404 for missing assets, Cache-Control (index no-cache, assets immutable), and precompressed br/gzip.
- MIME types are already correct via mime_guess (webmanifest is application/manifest+json, js is text/javascript). The web client already switches to wss: on https (api/client.ts:272).

Recommended HTTPS path: tailscale serve now (no code, a trusted certificate, all four device types have clients), or Caddy with tls internal if the owner does not want Tailscale. Later, engine-native TLS with a built-in local CA and a one-tap profile download for iPad/iPhone. For immediate use on the owner's own PC and MacBook in Chrome/Edge, the insecure-origin flag unlocks install and window-controls-overlay with no infrastructure.

Sources consulted: caniuse requestFullscreen; Apple Developer Forums thread 133248 (iOS element full screen); WebKit bugs 205917, 206854 and 212934; Apple support 104996 (Safari web apps on Mac); WWDC23 session 10120; heise and iDownloadBlog on iOS 26 Home Screen web apps; Mozilla support 'web-apps-firefox-windows'; MDN Keyboard.lock (secure context only) and Element.requestFullscreen.

summary:
I audited the UX and information architecture of OpenEtch's web UI. I read the code in web/src (App.tsx, the top bar, toolbar, menus, Modal, Laser dock, job controls, Viewport touch handling, Timeline, and all the CSS). I also checked the simulator's state over HTTP at 127.0.0.1:7979 (/api/machine, /api/documents, /api/prefs, the asset files and their headers). I did not use the browser pane, so pixel widths and heights are estimates from the CSS and should be checked at 375, 768, 1280x720 and 1470x870.

The base is strong:
- Fusion-style collapsible docks with a Window menu.
- A LightBurn-faithful editing model that uses pointer events.
- A Fusion-style timeline that shows who made each change (you, AI or script).
- Theme tokens in light and dark, reduced-motion support, and translated text.
- STOP lives in the top bar.

The main problems are layout density (built for 1920px+ screens), a missing app shell for full screen and installing as an app, safety status that is only visible inside the Laser panel, and touch support that maps the mouse model one-to-one.

Top UX improvements, in priority order:
1. **Keep STOP and the Design/Laser switch on screen at every width.** By the CSS sums, at 375–834px the right-hand group of the top bar overflows. STOP is clipped and the Design/Laser tabs shrink to almost nothing.
2. **Show machine state everywhere.** Add a top-bar status chip (Idle / Framing / Running 42% / Paused / Offline) with Pause and Stop frame, a banner when the connection drops, and refusal reasons shown inline in the Laser panel.
3. **Make Start a single flow.** Today the toolbar Start, the Alt+S hotkey and "Start here" skip the checklist UI and work from the Design workspace. The Start tooltip says Esc stops a burn, but it does not. There is no stop hotkey usable on a Mac or iPad keyboard.
4. **Rebuild the Design toolbar.** It is about 2,000px wide and scrolls sideways at every laptop width. Use Fusion-style groups (CREATE / MODIFY / ARRANGE / INSERT / INSPECT) plus a vertical LightBurn-style drawing-tool rail on the left.
5. **Cut the stacked bars from about 290px to about 170px on a MacBook.** Hide document tabs when only one document is open, use a compact toolbar, a collapsible 28px timeline, and one bottom bar that combines status, snapping, zoom and the palette. Make the side panels resizable and close the left one by default below 1440px.
6. **Add full screen and app-window support.** Add a web manifest (manifest.webmanifest and favicon.ico currently return the HTML page), app icons and theme-color, and a View > Full screen toggle (Fullscreen API, which works on plain http). Add Help text for Chrome/Edge "open as window", Safari "Add to Dock" and iPad "Add to Home Screen". Optional HTTPS on the Pi would enable install, Wake Lock and the browser camera.
7. **Make touch work properly.**
   - Selection modes on the canvas (Add/Toggle chips, and a marquee tool for touch).
   - Long-press opens the context menu.
   - Larger targets when the pointer is coarse, and compact rows on desktop.
   - On phones, use a bottom sheet instead of an 86%-wide drawer that opens on every tap.
8. **Restructure the menus.**
   - One menubar with submenus and arrow-key navigation, and a max-height on the File menu (about 30 items, so the bottom ones can't be reached on a MacBook).
   - Remove the duplicate entries (two Preferences items, Arrange as both a dropdown and a button grid).
   - Replace the toolbar's raw JSON Commands button with a Fusion-style "S" command search.
   - Turn the roughly 40-item context menu into short menus with submenus.
9. **Fix WCAG AA contrast.**
   - Muted text: 3.0–3.3:1 in light mode.
   - White text on blue buttons: 3.31 (light) and 2.67 (dark).
   - White text on the amber chip: 2.77 and 2.10.
   - STOP in dark mode: 3.49.
   - Input borders: 1.6:1.
10. **Build one dialog component.** It needs a focus trap, a dialog stack so Escape closes only the top dialog, no closing a form by tapping the backdrop, size variants, and full-screen sheets on phones.
11. **Onboarding.** Show a card on the empty canvas, and turn Beginner Mode into a curated toolbar plus a guided Preview → Frame → Start bar.
12. **Polish.** One icon set (Lucide, ISC licence, with Tabler, MIT, for CAD-specific icons), token scales for type, spacing and corner radius, compressed and cached assets, and lazy-loaded dialogs.

findings.problem: On phones and iPad portrait the top bar's right-hand group (.topbar-actions, flex:none) is wider than the window. STOP is the right-most item, so it is clipped. The Design/Laser switcher (.workspaces, min-width:0, overflow-x:auto) is the only item allowed to shrink, so it shrinks to almost nothing.
findings.evidence: styles.css: .topbar-actions {flex:none}; .topbar .workspaces {min-width:0; overflow-x:auto}; .app {overflow:hidden}. The right-hand group is Window menu (~74px), theme (34), gear (34), Help (~62), undo (34), redo (34), connection dot (~17), STOP (~86 incl. icon) and 7 gaps: about 407px at the <=480px rules, plus the File button (~50). That is about 475px against 375–430px phones. At 768px the actions are ~612px (the connection text 'Live · Laser connected' is still shown), leaving about 48px for brand + Design/Laser. Estimated from the CSS, not measured in a browser.
findings.recommendation: Give the top bar priority slots. STOP and the machine status chip are pinned on the right and never shrink. The workspace switch never drops below its content width (use a compact 'D | L' or icon segmented control on phones). Move theme, Preferences, Help, Window, undo and redo into a single overflow menu below about 900px; on touch, undo/redo can move to the canvas HUD. Add a regression check at 360, 375, 768 and 834px that STOP's bounding box is inside the viewport.

findings.problem:
The Design toolbar is about 2,000px wide and only scrolls sideways, so at 1280–1470px (MacBook) and even 1920px a large part is off-screen, including the Properties panel toggle at the far end. Its grouping mixes concerns:
- Import sits among the drawing tools, and drawing tools are split across three groups.
- 'Arrange' appears both as a dropdown and as a 16-button grid.
- 'Edit' is both a group name and a dropdown.
- 'Laser Tools' appears in the Design workspace.
- A developer 'Commands' (raw JSON) button is in both workspaces.
findings.evidence: Toolbar.tsx, EditMenus.tsx, useDesignUi.tsx toolbar, useTextTools.tsx toolbar and useLibsUi.tsx toolbar give about 24 .tool-btn (min-width calc(44px+20px*icon-scale) = 64px, labels at 11.5px) plus the 8x2 arrange grid (8x26px) and the snap grid. styles.css .toolbar {overflow-x:auto} with no wrap; tool-btn min-height 52px gives a toolbar row about 61px tall.

architecture_notes:
Proposed app shell (Fusion feel with LightBurn editing). This is a refactor of App.tsx's grid, not of the engine.

1. LayoutMode hook
   - Replace the single NARROW_QUERY with one hook that returns 'desktop' (≥1440), 'laptop' (1100–1439 or height <860), 'tablet' (700–1099, or a coarse pointer at any width) or 'phone' (<700), plus a `coarse` flag from (any-pointer: coarse).
   - Set data-layout and data-density attributes on <html> and drive all CSS from them. This removes the scattered 480/560/600/640/760/900 breakpoints.

2. Shell slots
   - AppBar (40px): ≡ menu or menubar, project name and dirty dot, doc tabs only when >1 document, the Design | Laser segmented control, the machine status chip, undo/redo, STOP (pinned, never inside an overflow menu).
   - CommandBar (40–44px): Fusion panels with caption dropdowns. Icon-only below 1440px, icon and label above.
   - ToolRail (40px, left, vertical): Select, the drawing tools, Text, Nodes, Trim, Measure. On phones it becomes a horizontal bottom tool strip.
   - Canvas with HUD: tool options bar (et-bar already exists), touch selection-mode chips, fit/zoom buttons, empty-state card.
   - Inspector (right; resizable 260–420px): Cuts/Layers and Properties as collapsible docks. On phones it becomes a bottom sheet with peek, half and full heights.
   - BottomBar (28–30px): coordinates, selection size, snap/grid/filled toggles and grid step (moved from the toolbar), zoom %, units, colour palette.
   - Timeline: collapsible strip (28px collapsed, 52px expanded).
   - The Laser workspace swaps the CommandBar for Preview | Frame ▾ | Start, and the Inspector shows the Laser dock first.

3. Shared stores and primitives
   - A machine/job status store (useJobStatus and machineState already exist; lift them to App) used by the AppBar chip, Laser dock, status bar and touch HUD.
   - One StartButton with startFlow(gates, scope) used by the toolbar, the hotkey, the dock and 'Start here'.
   - One Menu primitive: submenus, roving focus, type-ahead, max-height with scroll, long-press trigger. Used by the menubar, toolbar dropdowns, the Dock window menu and the context menu; replaces ContextMenu, DropMenu, useMenu (HelpMenu) and the WindowMenu ad-hoc menus.
   - One Dialog primitive: a stack manager for Escape/Enter, focus trap and restore, dismissable/dirty guard, sizes sm/md/lg/xl/full, and a sheet on phones. WsModal's stopPropagation becomes part of it.
   - A command registry: the hotkeys.ts ids plus labels and handlers (already partly there in ws.keymap.handlers). It feeds the menubar, the 'S' command search and the hotkey editor from one source, and is the natural surface for MCP parity.

4. Visual polish direction for a CAD tool
   - Font: system-ui stack ('Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', -apple-system, 'SF Pro Text', Inter, sans-serif), with tabular-nums for all numbers.
   - Type scale (px): 11 caption/hints, 12 labels/menus/inspector, 13 body/default, 15 section and dialog titles, 18 big stats (job progress). Weights 400/500/600 only. Uppercase only for 11px dock captions (letter-spacing .04em).
   - Spacing scale (4px base): 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 as --sp-0…--sp-6. Inspector rows use 8px vertical / 12px horizontal padding; groups are separated by 16px.
   - Density tokens:
     - fine pointer: --row-h 28px, --ctl-h 28px, --hit 28px, toolbar icon 20px.
     - coarse pointer: --row-h 40px, --ctl-h 40px, --hit 44px, icon 24px.
   - Corner radius: 2px (inputs inside groups, chips), 4px (buttons, fields), 8px (popovers, dialogs, sheets). Drop 3/6/9/10/18.
   - Elevation: 3 levels (popover, dialog, toast) as shadow tokens.
   - Z-index scale: base, dock-float, menu, dialog, toast, critical-banner.
   - Colour:
     - Neutral greys (Fusion), one blue accent for selection and focus.
     - Amber is reserved for 'laser armed/framing', red for STOP, errors and out-of-field, green for ready/OK, purple for AI-origin steps (already used).
     - Apply the AA token fixes from UX-09 and add a contrast unit test over the token table.
   - Icons: Lucide (ISC) with Tabler (MIT) for CAD-specific glyphs, inlined into one registry; 1.5 stroke at 20px.
   - Component patterns:
     - Fusion panel group (icon row plus caption ▾).
     - Split button (Frame ▾ with Box/Outline/Selection only).
